question: Should exec deny-over-allow policy live only in `exec-approvals.json`, or should OpenClaw permanently support and union both that store and `tools.exec.denylist` in `openclaw.json`?
rationale: Both designs are technically feasible, but choosing the supported persistence, precedence, migration, UI, protocol, and mixed-version contract is a product and security ownership decision that cannot be derived safely from the patch.

options.title: Use one approvals owner
options.body: Keep denylist policy in `exec-approvals.json` and remove the parallel `openclaw.json` surface, reducing configuration and compatibility complexity.

options.title: Sponsor dual ownership
options.body: Accept both persisted surfaces and explicitly document precedence, editing ownership, migration, protocol compatibility, and mixed-version behavior.

options.title: Decline the feature
options.body: Keep the existing deny, allowlist, and full modes unchanged and close the canonical feature request.

recommendation.title: Use one approvals owner
recommendation.body: Keep denylist policy in `exec-approvals.json` and remove the parallel `openclaw.json` surface, reducing configuration and compatibility complexity.
